question: When does the triad of will, knowledge, and action shine forth clearly as one?
premises: The triad belongs to the power-holder.
It appears through modes such as willing and so on.
The triad can appear either distinctly or in unity.
inference: When the triad shines forth in unity, it appears clearly as the power-holder's own integrated manifestation.
uncertainties: iṣyamāṇādikaiḥ is terse and may refer to will, knowledge, and action as modes.
plain_english: That same triad, through the power-holder's own modes such as willing and the rest, appears clearly; but when it shines forth in unity, then it does so as one.
